Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
5:24 AM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying as easy as sending a message, and it costs almost nothing to use.

Before UPI, small payments meant carrying cash, hunting for change, or typing long card and bank details. Now you scan a code or enter a phone number, type your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds, at any hour, even on holidays.

Free and instant: Most person-to-person and shop payments cost nothing, and the money arrives right away.
Works everywhere: From a tea stall to a big mall, one QR code takes payments from any bank's app, so shops don't need a card machine.
Simple and familiar: One phone and one PIN. No card, no cash, and even first-time smartphone users pick it up fast.

Shopkeepers like it too. There is no cash to count, no change to find, and every sale is recorded automatically. Once a few shops on a street accept UPI, the rest follow, and customers get used to paying this way very quickly.
